comment: The eleven languages the field asks about, one real file each, with the oracle that judges them.
**What the files are.** Seven of the eleven are source files fetched from a public repository at the ref named beside
them, kept in `benchmarks/polyglot/files/` so that the measurement runs offline and the bytes do not change under it.
**Five are this repository's own files**, which is a deliberate choice and not a convenience: a file written for this
measurement would be a file written to be parsed, and the least useful corpus there is. The ArkTS one is the
fixture the analyzer package already keeps for its own provider tests - ArkTS has no public corpus this project can
fetch, and the alternative was to write one, which would have measured the author rather than the scanner.
**What the oracle is.** `scripts/polyglot-oracle.mjs` reads the same file with a grammar somebody else wrote -
tree-sitter for the eight code languages, Python's `ElementTree` and `PyYAML` for XML and YAML - and answers the one
question both implementations can be asked: which names does this file declare at its top level. It does not compare
ranges, kinds or exports, because those are answers the two compute differently and a disagreement about them would
be a disagreement about the question.
**What this does not prove.** Recall here is against one file per language. **It is a measurement of the scanner and
not of the field**: an index that names every declaration in `JsonNull.java` has proved it reads Java, not that it
reads the Java a review meets. The field measurement is the martian artifact of §86, which is where the language
share is measured over 193 real changed paths.

**A second wave, and a different question.** The fourteen files above answer *does the scanner read this language at all*. The eleven below answer *does it read the constructs a reviewer files comments against* - an overload set, an annotation type, a merge key, a CDATA section - and they are written for this measurement, which is why they are marked `construct` rather than `fetched`. The author's expectation is not the truth in either wave: tree-sitter and ElementTree judge these too, so a fixture only has to *contain* the construct, and a disagreement is still a disagreement between two implementations.

files.why: The fetched Java file declares one class; this one declares a class, an interface, an enum, an annotation type and a base class, which is what recall needs to be able to fail on.
The fetched Swift file declares one type and one extension; this one declares a struct, a protocol, an enum, a class and three functions.
The fetched Groovy file declares one annotation type, which is the shape that exposed the @interface gap; this one declares four types.
ArkTS has no public corpus this project can fetch, and a file written for this measurement would measure its author.
Several top-level types in one file, a sealed hierarchy, a record with a compact constructor, an enum whose constants have bodies, an annotation type and a static initializer.
A sealed class with a nested data class and an object, a data class, an object with a @JvmStatic member, an annotation class, a value class, a typealias, a receiver function and a generic function.
A typealias, a protocol with an associated type, a struct with a static member, an enum with raw values, an extension, an attributed final class, an actor, an open class and a global let.
An annotation type, a trait, an enum, an abstract class, a @CompileStatic class with a static nested class, an untyped top-level method and a typed one.
Default export of a class, a generator, an async generator, a class with private fields and a private method, a subclass and a destructuring-free arrow.
An overload set (two signatures and one body), a re-export, a const enum, a namespace, a declared module, an abstract class and a default export.
Decorated sync and async functions, a nested class, a property, a module constant and a module-level dict annotation.
A @Component struct with @State and @Prop fields, an @Entry struct, a @Builder function and an exported class and interface.
A key with a colon in it, a key with an escaped quote, a non-ASCII key, four levels of nesting, an array of objects, an empty object and an empty array.
An anchor and a merge key, a block scalar whose body looks like keys, a flow mapping, a quoted key containing a colon, a sequence of maps and a second document.

A DOCTYPE with an internal subset, a processing instruction, a default namespace and a prefixed one, a comment containing a tag, a CDATA section containing a tag and an attribute with an escaped greater-than.
